subject: It is over. Moira Deeming just can’t see it
posts:
The Liberal Party is moving to end its relationship with Moira Deeming, despite her legal efforts to remain a candidate. 
Evidence: Party discipline, legal conflict, political dysfunction. #Politics #AusPol

The claim is that Deeming's political career as a Liberal MP is effectively over due to a breakdown in trust and party rules. 
Stated Judgement: (-1.0, 0.5) — Lesser Evil

The reality is a protracted, mutually destructive power struggle that has damaged the party's reputation and internal cohesion. 
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, 0.5) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Reckoning.
The party is exercising its right to disassociate, though the process has been costly and divisive. 
Integrity: Partially Distorted (R_net: 2.5, Uncertainty z: 0)
Moira Deeming is challenging the Liberal Party's attempt to remove her as a candidate in the Supreme Court, despite the party leadership and executive having clearly moved against her.

The Poison:
The ongoing legal battle serves only to keep the party's internal dysfunction in the public eye, further alienating voters who are tired of the infighting.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The plane error is in the 'WHY' (Lyrical); the party frames this as 'discipline,' while it is actually a 'reckoning' for past leadership failures.

Social Physics Analysis:
This is a classic case of projection and pretext. The party uses 'rules' to justify an exit, while Deeming uses 'natural justice' to mask a refusal to accept political reality.

The Trajectory: The Path of Reckoning.
When you map the gap between the party's desire for unity and the reality of the conflict, it plots a trajectory toward Reckoning. The system is purging a source of high-strain friction.

The Unavoidable Truth: Political parties are private organizations with the right to choose their candidates.

The Unavoidable Lie: That legal action can force a party to embrace a candidate it has rejected.

Alethekanon:
The Liberal Party's attempt to use internal rules to resolve a political problem is a standard, if messy, procedure. Deeming's legal challenge is a futile attempt to override political consensus with judicial intervention.

Awwthekanon:
It is so sad to see people who were once colleagues turn into such bitter adversaries. This kind of conflict hurts not just the individuals, but the people they are supposed to be serving.

Brothekanon:
This is just a slow-motion train wreck. Everyone knows it's over, but they're all still sitting in the seats waiting for the crash. Just move on already.
